whyChoose.title: What California Law Means for Your Claim

items.title: A Filing Clock Is Already Running
items.desc: California generally gives you two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity was involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months, so timing matters.

items.title: Being Partly at Fault Doesn't End Your Claim
items.desc: Under California's pure comparative fault rule, you can still recover damages even if you were partly responsible for what happened. Your share of fault simply reduces the amount you might be owed, it doesn't erase it.

items.title: No Ceiling on Non-Economic Damages
items.desc: In an ordinary injury case, California places no cap on compensation for pain, suffering, and other non-economic losses. That means your claim isn't artificially limited by a fixed dollar amount.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That structure lets you get legal help without worrying about hourly bills.

items.answer: Nothing. LawProactive is a free service that connects you with an independent attorney in Lake County. There's no charge to have your situation reviewed, and no obligation to move forward.

items.question: Is LawProactive a law firm?
items.answer: No. We're a connection service, not a law firm. We introduce injured people to independent personal injury attorneys who can evaluate their case and advise on next steps.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim in California?
items.answer: Most injury claims must be filed within two years of the incident. If your injury involved a government vehicle or property, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's worth checking sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly responsible for the accident?
items.answer: California follows a pure comparative fault rule, meaning partial fault reduces your compensation but doesn't automatically bar you from recovering. An attorney can help sort out how fault might apply to your situation.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to cluster in Clearlake?
items.answer: Public records show injury collisions occurring along corridors like Rt 53, Lakeshore Drive, Old Highway 53, and Olympic Drive, with reports tending to peak on Fridays between 2 and 4 p.m. These are neutral collision counts, not a judgment about any particular road.
